A_target.statement:
Let $G = \struct {L, R, E}$ be a [[Definition:Bipartite Graph|bipartite graph]].
Then a [[Definition:Maximum Matching|maximum matching]] of $G$ can be computed, and its size equals the value of a [[Definition:Maximum Flow|maximum flow]] in an associated network.

B_source.statement:
Let $N$ be a [[Definition:Flow Network|flow network]] with [[Definition:Integer|integer]] capacities.
Then $N$ has an integral [[Definition:Maximum Flow|maximum $s$-$t$ flow]], computable by the [[Ford-Fulkerson Algorithm]].

object_map.reformulation: Encode G as a unit-capacity flow network with added source s and sink t.

validity_conditions: All capacities are 1, so an integral flow selects a set of edges with no shared endpoint (a matching). This is the load-bearing condition.
Integrality of the max flow (guaranteed for integer capacities) — a fractional flow would not correspond to a matching.
proof_plan: Build the network $N$: an arc $s \to u$ of capacity $1$ for each $u \in L$, an arc $v \to t$ of capacity $1$ for each $v \in R$, and an arc $u \to v$ of capacity $1$ for each $u v \in E$.
By the [[Integral Flow Theorem]], compute an integral maximum flow $f$.

As all capacities are $1$, each $u \in L$ sends flow along at most one arc and each $v \in R$ receives along at most one.
Hence the saturated arcs $u \to v$ form a [[Definition:Matching (Graph Theory)|matching]].
Conversely each matching gives a flow of the same value.
